subject: Follow-up: Cost targets & latency trade-offs (tokens / $/1M)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@synthhealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@synthhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Cost targets & latency trade-offs (tokens / $/1M)

Hi Alex & Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and asks so we can turn this into a scoped POC and a pricing proposal: 

- What we heard: high accuracy for clinical summarization + embeddings for search. Target 99.9th p95 latency for UI flows, and an async batch pipeline for nightly indexing.
- Actionable asks for proposal: 
  1) Estimated token volume: average tokens per inference and daily/monthly totals (we know these are estimates — ranges are fine).
  2) Target budget band (monthly committed or target $/1M tokens you want to aim for).
  3) Latency SLOs: which routes need streaming (sub-250ms) vs batch (multi-second ok).

To make this concrete, could you reply with rough low/typical/high token volume and a preferred $/1M target (or monthly budget range) by EOD Friday? We can then propose model tiering + batch/stream settings that fit your budget and SLOs.

Attaching a short spreadsheet that maps $/1M token bands to recommended model tiers and batch settings (very high-level).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@synthhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost targets & latency trade-offs (tokens / $/1M)

Thanks Soojin — quick answers below. Priya is looped for validation.

- Token volumes: our first POC will have two workloads: 
  • Interactive summaries (UI): ~1.5k tokens per request average, 6k reqs/day => ~9M tokens/day (peak 15M).
  • Nightly indexing (batch): ~200k tokens per run, once per day => ~200k tokens/day.
  Rough monthly (30d) expected range: 180M (low) - 450M (high) tokens.

- Budget: initial target is to be in the $800 - $1,400 / 1M tokens range for POC economics. We are flexible if there are clear latency trade-offs.

- Latency SLOs: UI flows need p95 <= 300ms ideally (sub-250 preferred for critical path). Nightly batch has no tight SLO (minutes acceptable).

Let us know whattiers and batching you'd recommend given those numbers. Also, we have security questions — Priya will send a short questionnaire separately.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Product Manager
SynthHealth Inc.
alex.turner@synthhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@synthhealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@synthhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost targets & latency trade-offs (tokens / $/1M)

Alex — great detail, thanks. Short recommendation based on the volume and your budget target: 

1) Model tiering (hybrid routing):
   - UI (latency-sensitive): Redwood Dedicated low-latency tier using a smaller but faster quantized variant for interactive requests to hit ~200-300ms p95. This will increase $/1M compared to max-quantized batch models, so we'll target ~$1,200 / 1M for UI tokens in initial POC.
   - Batch indexing: use high-efficiency quantized models with 4-bit kernels and large-batch execution to hit < $400 / 1M for the nightly workload.

2) Batching & streaming settings:
   - Enable streaming on UI routes with small dynamic batching windows (10-30ms) to keep tail latencies down.
   - Nightly pipeline: aggressive batching (sequence packing) and KV cache warmup to maximize throughput.

3) SLO-driven pricing note: we can offer a blended price for the POC: 
   - Blended target: $900 / 1M tokens (weighted by expected volume: UI heavy). This is conditional on a 3-month POC commit and a single model family. If you need sub-250ms p95 on 99.9% of requests under peak, there is a $/1M uplift we should budget for (we estimate +20% for guaranteed tails).

4) Next steps I propose:
   - Redwood sends a short POC statement of work + pricing tiers (we'll include line items for streaming premium and batch-efficiency discounts).
   - SynthHealth confirms PO/commit range or a budget band.
   - Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence exchange (Priya to send the form).

Attaching a short PDF that outlines latency vs cost trade-offs and example blended math.

— Karthik
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: slo-latency-options.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@synthhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@synthhealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost targets & latency trade-offs (tokens / $/1M)

Thanks Karthik — that blended math looks reasonable. A couple clarifying points before we sign: 

- If we target the blended $900 / 1M (with the UI premium baked in), what are the specific throttles or burst limits during peak hours? We anticipate some batch-like spikes from concurrent users during morning sync windows.
- On the +20% uplift for guaranteed tails: can you provide an example SLA clause that describes the measurement window (p95 over 30 days vs rolling 7-day) and the failure remediation (credits or fallback policies)?

We can commit to a 3-month POC budget band if you include a capped overage policy and a list of required SOC2 items. Priya will forward the security questionnaire today.

Also, please send the POC SoW and the DocuSign link when ready.

Regards,
Alex

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Alex/Priya — perfect, we can do that. Quick commitments from our side: 

- We'll include a 30% burst allowance over committed throughput for the POC (soft throttle after that with notifications).
- SLA sample: p95 measured daily and reported as a 7-day rolling window; remediation as service credit tiers up to X% of monthly POC fee for missed objectives (we'll include precise language in the SoW).
- We'll send the POC SoW and a DocuSign link by tomorrow morning.

Attachments included: finalized pricing spreadsheet and draft SoW. Once Priya sends the security questionnaire we'll route it to compliance and provide the SOC2/pen-test artifacts.

Next steps for SynthHealth: reply to this thread with the preferred monthly budget band to lock the blended price, and Priya to attach the security questionnaire.
